handbookNote: South Carolina Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- South Carolina previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only sc_re_salesperson (Associate). Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the South Carolina Real Estate Commission (Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly reading PSI's own official South Carolina Real Estate Candidate Information Bulletin (bulletin id 441, updated 8/27/2026) -- SC's PSI landing page (test-takers.psiexams.com/scre) had no direct bulletin link (unlike NJ/MN), requiring navigation through PSI's test-taker SPA (View Available Tests -> the 'SC Broker' test card -> its Test Details page) to find the real 'Candidate Bulletin' link. Exam Summary Table, quoted directly from the bulletin: Broker exam = National portion 75 items (80 points possible -- national broker exams include questions scored up to two points, disclosed here rather than silently flattened), 120 minutes; State portion 50 items (50 points), 80 minutes; combined 125 items (130 points), 200-minute time limit. Passing, quoted directly from the bulletin's own Score Reporting table (Broker row): National Portion 60 (of 80 points), State Portion 36 (of 50) -- both portions independently scored and both must be passed; 96 of 125 combined items = 76.8%. This site's track_registry schema models one combined row rather than two separately-scored portions, so the DB row records combined totals (125 questions, 12000s/200min duration, 76.8% pass, min_correct=96 matching the bulletin's own two-portion point totals added together) -- the real two-portion, two-timer, separately-scored structure is disclosed in the track's own description/mechanicsNote copy instead. A small number of 5-10 unscored experimental items may also appear, not counted against the 125. CONTENT OUTLINE -- National portion percentages, quoted verbatim from the bulletin (Broker column, summing to exactly 100% of the 75-item national portion, independently re-verified by hand this session): Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19% (the largest single national topic), Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5% (Broker-only sub-items), Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12% (Broker-only supervisory sub-items), Real Estate Calculations 6%. NOTABLE: these percentages are IDENTICAL to every other PSI-administered state in this campaign (NJ/TN/VA/AZ/MA/MO/MN) -- yet further confirmation PSI uses one shared multi-state National Portion content-outline template for real estate broker exams nationwide. South Carolina State portion, quoted verbatim as item counts (of the 50-item state portion, Broker column, summing to the full 50): South Carolina Real Estate Commission and Licensing Requirements 10 items (Commission Purpose/Powers/Duties; Activities Requiring a License and Exemptions; License Types/Maintenance/Duration/Statuses/Changes); Statutes Governing the Activities of Licensees and Non-Licensees 16 items (the largest state bucket -- Advertising; Broker/Associate/Non-Licensee Relationships; Commissions and Other Compensation; Disclosure of Licensee's Interest; Offers and Counteroffers; Handling of Documents and Record Keeping; Handling of Monies and Accounting Practices; License Law Violations/Investigations/Penalties); South Carolina Agency and Non-agency Relationships and Issues 13 items (Permissible Relationships and Obligations to Parties; Disclosure Requirements and Issues; Creation and Termination of Agency; SC Agency and Non-agency Contracts); Additional South Carolina Statutes and Topics 7 items (Consumer Protection Code, Homestead Exemption, Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Vacation Rental Act and Time Sharing Plan Act, Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statements, SC Fair Housing Law, SC Smoke Detector Law); Closing Details 4 items. This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, PSI-published weights, not an even split -- actual per-bucket counts were then set by each drafting pass to whatever its real, verifiable source material actually supported, with NO target number or ceiling given to any drafting pass, per this campaign's corrected policy (see mo_re_broker.json for the incident writeup). Real South Carolina statute/case-law facts independently verified this session via scstatehouse.gov (South Carolina's official State House code-of-laws site) -- S.C. Code Ann. Title 40, Chapter 57 (Real Estate Brokers, Salesmen, and Property Managers License Law), including live-fetched provisions such as Sec. 40-57-10/-40/-60 (Commission creation/composition/powers), Sec. 40-57-20/-30/-240 (license requirement, compensation-based broker/associate definitions, statutory exemptions), Sec. 40-57-110/-115/-120/-310/-320/-330/-345 (license classifications, background checks, residency-change notice, age/experience/education requirements, single broker-in-charge affiliation, CE exemption), Sec. 40-57-135/-136 (advertising, broker-in-charge duties, trust account titling/commingling/48-hour deposit-timing rules, offers/counteroffers, licensee-interest disclosure, recordkeeping), Sec. 40-57-330 (broker-in-charge licensure), Sec. 40-57-710 through -790 (the full disciplinary grounds/investigation/fine/revocation framework, including a 2024 Act No. 204 amendment raising the disciplinary fine cap to $10,000), Sec. 40-57-30 and 40-57-350 (the five real, statutorily-defined SC brokerage relationships -- seller agency, buyer agency, disclosed dual agency, designated agency, transaction brokerage -- and their fiduciary/non-fiduciary duty structures), Sec. 40-57-135(J) (designated agency signing-timing rules); Title 37 (Consumer Protection Code); Title 15, Chapter 41, Article 1 (Homestead Exemption, real dollar caps -- $50,000/$100,000-married/$50,000-per-spouse -- and vehicle exemption, plus the clerk-of-court deposit mechanic); Title 27, Chapter 40 (Residential Landlord and Tenant Act -- deposit itemization/30-day return, treble-damages penalty, habitability, 5-day/14-day cure notices, 30-day month-to-month termination, retaliation protection, owner-identity disclosure); Title 27, Chapter 50, Article 2 (Vacation Rental Act) and Title 27, Chapter 32, Article 1 (Time Sharing Plan Act, Broker only -- 90-day rental definition, trust accounting, title-transfer obligations, 5-day timeshare cancellation right, SC REC registration, escrow requirements); Title 27, Chapter 50, Article 1 (Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement -- 1-4 unit scope, delivery timing, exemptions, owner/licensee liability allocation); Title 31, Chapter 21 (SC Fair Housing Law -- protected classes, familial status, steering, owner-occupied exemption, South Carolina Human Affairs Commission enforcement, 180-day filing deadline); Title 5, Chapter 25, Sec. 5-25-1310 et seq. (South Carolina's real smoke-detector transfer-affidavit statute for one/two-family dwellings -- confirmed live that Title 23 Chapter 9's State Fire Marshal Law only covers apartment buildings generically and contains nothing about real estate transfers, so Title 5 Ch. 25 was used instead as the genuinely applicable citation); and, for Closing Details, South Carolina's real attorney-only-closing rule (State v. Buyers Service Co., holding that conducting a residential closing constitutes the practice of law in South Carolina and may only be performed by a licensed SC attorney) plus Title 12, Chapter 24 (the $1.85-per-$500 deed recording fee, split $0.55 county / $1.30 state under Sec. 12-24-10/-20/-40/-90) and Title 12, Chapter 37/43 (property tax assessment, the 15% cap on most annual taxable-value increases, and Sec. 12-43-220's county equalization/reassessment mechanics). Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math content not tied to a South Carolina-specific statute is sourced to 'national real estate practice principles' framing throughout. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate. This bank was drafted across 16 parallel single-topic drafting passes (11 national + 5 South Carolina state-law categories, mirroring MN's one-per-topic model), each pass instructed to draft as many genuinely distinct, real, grounded questions as its topic's source material supports with NO target number or ceiling. Two of the 16 topics (Additional South Carolina Statutes and Topics, Closing Details) were delayed by a platform concurrent-subagent cap and a session rate-limit hit respectively -- the Closing Details agent's session was cut off by a rate limit after it had ALREADY finished writing its 11-question file, so no work was lost; that file was used as-is since 4 of 50 state items is a genuinely narrow topic and 11 questions honestly exhausts its two real sub-areas (attorney-only closings, deed recording fee/property tax mechanics) without padding. A cross-bucket source_note-citation dedup check across all 16 files found ZERO cross-bucket near-duplicates, matching Minnesota's and Maryland's clean results earlier in this campaign. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_sc_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 16 bucket files combined, in file order), producing a final near-even 25.1/25.1/24.9/24.9% A/B/C/D distribution. 618 raw questions drafted against a 125-item exam -- a 4.94:1 pool ratio, comfortably clearing the standing 4:1 new-track floor and landing just under the 5:1 project-wide aspiration, with no backfill pass needed.
